title: Orientation invariance conjecture for s-permutree lattices
source: Eva Philippe and Vincent Pilaud, “Geometric realizations of the s-weak order and its lattice quotients”, arXiv:2405.02092 (v4, 2025), Conjecture 76. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.02092)

lanes.review: shard016-candidate-review-opus-20261119-r1/REVIEW-362959.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS, FLAGS none; required the literal lattice-theoretic endpoint)
lanes.final_paper_definition_and_prior_art_che: final-paper-check-362959-opus-20261119-r1/CHECK-362959.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; revised paper used)

significance.root_decision: For every n, every tuple s of non-negative integers (zero entries allowed), every decoration of the other positions and every position k decorated up, changing the decoration at k from up to down changes neither the number of elements of the delta-permutree lattice (the quotient of the s-weak order by the lattice congruence generated by the decoration) nor, for any m, the number of faces of size m of its canonical join complex. This is Conjecture 76 of Philippe and Pilaud. Lean formalizes the objects literally: s-trees and their order with a proved lattice structure, s-arcs, the generated congruence (proved to contract exactly the forbidden arcs), the quotient lattice and canonical join representations defined lattice-theoretically; the proof identifies faces with marked arc diagrams by a sweep bijection and proves the forward direction of the source's Theorem 72 by a direct congruence construction.
significance.caveat: Bounded literature search only. A later paper on framing lattices (von Bell and Ceballos, arXiv:2512.20575) covers the s-weak order and classical permutree lattices but not s-permutree lattices or this conjecture; it suggests a possible alternative route that is not published. The case s = (1,...,1) is close to a known classical statement (Pilaud-Pons 2018, cardinality only).

root_basis: Root extracted the thirty-two modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, axioms exactly the allowed three, no forbidden tokens), and screened the Principia archive (300 ids), the omega registry and GitHub by id. An independent Opus referee compared each Lean definition with the source, transcribed the Lean definitions into Python and compared cardinalities and f-vectors with a computation from the source definitions on 32,547 instances (all agree, including the source's worked example), checked that no definition collapses, re-derived the new proof of the forward direction of Theorem 72, and supplied the revised paper used here.
